segments.he: מִי שֶׁאֲחָזוֹ קוּרְדְּיָיקוֹס, וְאָמַר: ״כִּתְבוּ גֵּט לְאִשְׁתִּי״ – לֹא אָמַר כְּלוּם. אָמַר: ״כִּתְבוּ גֵּט לְאִשְׁתִּי״, וַאֲחָזוֹ קוּרְדְּיָיקוֹס, וְחָזַר וְאָמַר: ״לֹא תִּכְתְּבֶנּוּ״ – אֵין דְּבָרָיו הָאַחֲרוֹנִים כְּלוּם.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «one who was afflicted with» temporary «insanity [kordeyakos] and said: Write a bill of divorce for my wife, he said nothing,» because he was not lucid at the time. If «he said: Write a bill of divorce for my wife,» when he was lucid, «and was» then «afflicted with» temporary «insanity and he retracted» his previous statement «and said: Do not write it, his latter statement» is considered to be «nothing,» i.e., it is not halakhically valid.

segments.he: נִשְׁתַּתֵּק, וְאָמְרוּ לוֹ: ״נִכְתּוֹב גֵּט לְאִשְׁתְּךָ״, וְהִרְכִּין בְּרֹאשׁוֹ – בּוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ שְׁלֹשָׁה פְּעָמִים, אִם אָמַר עַל לָאו – ״לָאו״, וְעַל הֵן – ״הֵן״, הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ יִכְתְּבוּ וְיִתְּנוּ.
segments.en: The mishna continues: In a case where the husband «became mute, and» two people «said to him:» Shall «we write a bill of divorce for your wife, and he nodded his head» indicating his agreement, «they examine him» with various questions «three times. If he responded to» questions that have «a negative» answer: «No, and» responded «to» questions that have «a positive» answer: «Yes,» indicating his competence, «they shall write» the bill of divorce «and give» it to his wife based on the nod of his head.

moves.summary: Instruction during temporary insanity is void; a later insane retraction is void
A mute husband is tested three times by yes/no questions

positions.claim: Instruction given during kordeyakos is void; a lucid instruction is not revoked by a retraction during it
A mute husband who nods is examined three times; if his answers are consistent, they write and give
